ceiling_directive: Resolve the universal finite-switch question by completing the two-cycle constrained-Hessian test and proving an explicit parameter-uniform piece bound yielding an exact finite optimization for both active-ceiling envelopes.
improvement_directive: Prove or refute the universal finite-switch representation for the active-ceiling one-bin problem, including the saturated-nuisance, negative-multiplier regime. If affirmative, give an explicit bound B and prove equality of the finite-piece program with H_z and h_z across all normal, singular, abnormal, flat, and boundary cases.
critique: The advertised exact active-ceiling frontier is not derived: H_z and h_z remain infinite-dimensional supremum and infimum definitions, while the universal finite-switch representation and optimizer characterization are left open. The sharp backward recursion is valid but does not make those local envelopes evaluable, so the project's claim that it constructs the active-ceiling frontier overstates what is delivered. The matched worst-case mesh-width order, compatibility characterization, inactive-ceiling formula, and abstract interval sharpness form a worthwhile specialized contribution, but they do not replace the missing active-ceiling kernel. The confidence inversion is likewise only formally specified because no exact endpoint algorithm or certified approximation scheme is supplied, and the absence of an application or reproducible active-ceiling computation further limits the projected paper score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.4 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
